title.narrative: Peshawar Sustainable Bus Rapid Transit Corridor Project

description.narrative: The proposed project will help develop a sustainable urban transport system in Peshawar by delivering the city's first integrated BRT corridor, directly benefiting 0.5 million people. The project will comprise two interlinked outputs: (i) the construction of a 26-kilometer (km) BRT corridor and associated facilities, and (ii) effective project management and sustainable BRT operations through institutional developments. The project is economically justified by major time savings for future BRT passengers, vehicle operating cost savings, better air quality, and carbon emissions savings, which will improve the health of Peshawar's citizens and mitigate climate change. The project will also make Peshawar more livable and safe, boost private sector investment, and foster gender equity.

Quality of public transport in Peshawar improved, benefiting a population of half a million

Annual GHG emissions (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide, and halocarbons) reduced by 31,000 metric tons due to public transport vehicles' modernization Progress/Status: The current ridership shows that mode shifting from private modes have occurred. In addition, the plug-in hybrid electric vehicles have enhanced vehicle efficiency and the accompanying emission reductions. To determine the actual annual reduction in GHG emissions, a study will be conducted upon the completion of the Project (when all buses are in operation and all depots are operationalized). Data Source: KPUMA statistics Actual value:

BRT daily ridership reaches 480,000 passengers, of whom 20% are women. Progress/Status: Achieved: 66% The daily ridership reached approximately 320,000 passenger-trips in January 2023. Due to one of the deposits still being constructed, the system is operating with 220 buses as originally planned and without two of the direct service routes in operation. The second depot is scheduled for completion by Q3 2023, at which time the additional buses and services will be operated. On average, the estimated percentage of women using buses is 26% which is well above the baseline of 15%. Data Source: TransPeshawar and bus service providers' progress reports Actual value:

Modern BRT buses operating at a maximum 5 minute headway over a 80-km total network Progress/Status: Achieved: 100% BRT system began custom operations in August 2020. The current system encompasses 28 kilometers of dedicated busway services and over 60 kilometers of direct off-corridor routes. Headway of buses is adjusted to ensure that frequency is less than 5 mins at every bus station. Data Source: TransPeshawar and bus service providers' progress reports Actual value:
